children.text: Rising to about

, Mayon Volcano is the Philippines' most active volcano, famous for its near-perfect conical shape. Climbing it is prohibited, but its majestic form can be admired up close from all over Albay province, at the Cagsawa Ruins, Ligñon Hill, and the ATV lava trails.
Mayon Volcano is a stratovolcano rising to about

in Albay province, in the Bicol region of southeastern Luzon. It rises in an almost perfectly symmetrical cone from the plains near the sea, earning it the title of "the world's most perfect volcanic cone." Its name is said to come from magayon, the Bicolano word for "beautiful," and a legend about a beautiful woman named Daragang Magayon is woven into the mountain's story.
Despite its beauty, Mayon is the most active volcano in the Philippines. More than 50 eruptions have been recorded since the 17th century. The great eruption of
February 1, 1814
buried nearby villages under pyroclastic flows and ash, killing over 1,000 people, and its traces remain today as the Cagsawa Ruins. Further eruptions followed in
, and
Mayon remained active in
as well. After the alert level rose to Level 2 on
January 1
, the lava dome at the summit collapsed repeatedly, and on
January 6
the level went up to 3, with several thousand residents of Albay province evacuated. On
May 2
lava flowed about
3.8 km
down the Basud Gully, and activity was strongest on
July 11–18
. After the lava flow stopped on
July 22
, the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) lowered the alert to Level 2 on
August 5, 2026
, but because sulfur dioxide emissions were high, ash was still emitted from the summit on the morning of
October 3
. Regardless of the alert level, the area within a
6 km
radius of the summit is a Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ) and entry is prohibited, and ordinary tourists are currently not permitted to climb to the summit.

So a Mayon trip isn't about "climbing" — it's about "viewing." You can see Mayon from a different angle at almost every stop: downtown Legazpi, the Cagsawa Ruins, Ligñon Hill, and the lakes and hills of Camalig, and an ATV tour across the volcano's lava fields at its base is also very popular. It suits travelers who want to combine majestic natural scenery, spicy Bicolano food, and Spanish-era churches and ruins.
Mayon's slopes span eight cities and municipalities in Albay province, and Albay Gulf is about
10 km
away. The summit crater is about
in diameter. On
it was designated the Philippines' first national park, in
it was renamed Mayon Volcano Natural Park, and in

it was inscribed by UNESCO as the core of the Albay Biosphere Reserve. Radiating lava gullies, carved by the lava that flowed down with each eruption, cut into the slopes, and in heavy rain these gullies become paths for mudflows (lahars). In fact, in late
November 2006
, torrential rain from Typhoon Durian (locally named Reming) swept volcanic deposits downhill, leaving more than 1,000 people dead or missing.

blocks.title: View Mayon from the Cagsawa Ruins

children.text: The bell tower of a church destroyed in the
eruption, with Mayon rising behind it, is one of the Philippines' most iconic photo compositions. It's best visited early in the morning, before clouds settle over the summit.
ATV tours departing from the road at the entrance to the Cagsawa Ruins vary by route, from a meadow course of
30 minutes
(about
) to a lava trail of
3–4 hours
(about
). Operators such as Mayon SkyDrive provide safety instruction and helmets, and riders aged 16 and over can drive themselves. Departing at
7–8 AM

, when the summit is most visible, is recommended. Riding across hardened lava fields and volcanic gullies lets you feel Mayon at its closest, but routes are restricted depending on the alert level. In
January 2026
, routes inside the 6 km zone were closed and tours ran only within the Cagsawa area.
A hilltop park in Bogtong village, about
3 km
west of Legazpi Port, where the summit viewpoint takes in Mayon, Legazpi's cityscape, and Albay Gulf in a single view. Opening hours are
, and sources disagree on the entrance fee, ranging from free to about
. There is a zipline (about

), a suspension bridge, a tunnel dug by Japanese forces during World War II, and a viewpoint cafe, and sunset is especially lovely. The park is being renovated, so check which facilities are operating before you go.
Built from volcanic stone in
, this Baroque church stands on a hill, and from its front steps Mayon appears directly in view. Its intricately carved facade is also worth a look.
The Legazpi Boulevard, running along Albay Gulf, is popular with locals for jogging and strolling. The view of Mayon across the water, especially at sunset, is beautiful.
A spot where you can view Mayon from a bamboo raft gliding across a calm lake. The volcano's reflection on the water has made this a popular photo spot.
Try the spicy flavors of the Bicol region: Bicol Express, made with coconut milk and chili; laing, taro leaves simmered in coconut milk; Camalig's signature pinangat; and even chili ice cream.
During active periods, the red glow of lava at the summit can sometimes be seen at night from downtown Legazpi or safe viewpoints. Only observe from areas officially designated as safe.

Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific fly from Manila to Bicol International Airport (DRP) in Daraga, Albay, about
1 hour

. There are also direct flights from Cebu. From the airport to downtown Legazpi is about
30–40 minutes

Buses to Legazpi depart daily from the Cubao, Pasay, and PITX terminals in Manila. Several companies, including DLTB and Raymond, run the route; the trip takes about
12–14 hours

depending on class. Buses arrive at the Legazpi Grand Central Terminal. Philtranco, which ran this route for many years, stopped service on
March 30, 2026
, so don't go looking for it based on older guides. An overnight bus gets you to Legazpi in the morning.

items.title: From Bicol International Airport to the city

children.text: Bicol International Airport is in Daraga, about
15 km
from downtown Legazpi, and opened in
to replace the old Legazpi Airport. Airport vans leave once they are full and cost about
to downtown Legazpi and about
to Daraga. Grab starts at about
to the city, and if you take a taxi, make sure the meter is running. You can also book a hotel pickup or a private car (from about
US$45
for 4 people).

items.title: Cebu, Naga, Donsol, and driving yourself

children.text: From Cebu Mactan, Cebu Pacific group airlines fly nonstop to Bicol International Airport only on certain days of the week, so check the days when you book. From
Naga City
it takes about
2 hours 30 minutes–3 hours
by bus or van to Legazpi. From
Donsol
it is about
1 hour 30 minutes
by van, and the last van leaves before evening, so check your return time in advance.
By road, Legazpi is about
500 km
from Manila, taking the South Luzon Expressway (SLEX) onto the Maharlika Highway (Pan-Philippine Highway) and passing Lucena and Naga. Buses take more than
12 hours
for the trip, so if you're driving yourself, it's safer to stay a night in Naga or another stop along the way.
Jeepneys and vans run frequently between downtown Legazpi, Daraga, and Camalig, with fares of about
. The Cagsawa Ruins are about
30 minutes
from Legazpi by jeepney — take a Daraga-bound jeepney and get off at the Cagsawa entrance, then transfer to a tricycle. To cover several sights in a day, a half-day tricycle charter (about
) or a full-day van charter with driver (about
) is convenient.
Unlike western Luzon, the Bicol region has a short dry season and sees rain year-round. The relatively drier, clearer period from
February
to
May
is the best time to see Mayon.
March–April
especially has many mornings when the summit is visible without a cloud.
From
June
to
December
, typhoons and the northeast monsoon bring frequent rain, and in
September–December
strong typhoons often pass through the Bicol region. Heavy rain increases the risk of lahar (volcanic mudflow) washing down the volcano's slopes, sometimes suspending ATV tours.
The time of day matters for Mayon, too. The summit usually starts to be hidden by clouds after
, so the best viewing is from just after sunrise until
8 AM
. Albay province holds the "Magayon Festival" around
May
, and Legazpi City holds the "Ibalong Festival" around
August
, with street parades and performances.
Legazpi's average monthly temperature is about
in
January
, the coolest month, and about
in the hottest months,
May–June
, and annual rainfall reaches about 3,600 mm. It is hot and humid all year, and showers pass through even in the dry season, so bring a raincoat. In
February
, the Cagsawa Festival, commemorating the 1814 eruption, is held around the Cagsawa Ruins.

The base for a Mayon trip is Legazpi, the capital of Albay province. There are many mid-range hotels around the city center and coastal boulevard, priced around
per night, and some hotels offer "Mayon view" rooms — worth confirming when you book. For a quieter setting, small resorts and guesthouses in Daraga or Camalig are also good options.

Bicolano food generously uses coconut milk and chili. Signature dishes include Bicol Express, pork simmered in coconut milk and chili; laing, taro leaves stewed in coconut milk; and pinangat from Camalig, shrimp and coconut milk wrapped and steamed in taro leaves. The long-running restaurant 1st Colonial Grill in Legazpi is famous for its chili ice cream, a unique dessert combining spiciness and sweetness. For souvenirs, cookies and candy made from Bicol's specialty pili nuts are popular.

Choose your lodging according to your purpose. Downtown Legazpi is convenient for getting around, with restaurants, malls, and terminals close by; if you have an early flight, Daraga, home to Bicol International Airport, is handy; and if you're after sunrise photography and ATV rides, the Busay area, where the Cagsawa Ruins are located, is advantageous. If you want a room with a view of Mayon, choose a hotel that advertises Mayon-view rooms on its official site, such as The Oriental Legazpi. Downtown has SM City Legazpi and Ayala Malls, where you can handle currency exchange, ATMs, and meals in one stop, and in the evening the area around the coastal boulevard is a good place for seafood and Bicolano food. If spicy food is a concern, choose laing without chili or grilled fish.
Before visiting, check PHIVOLCS's official announcements for the current alert level and restricted zones. Depending on the alert level, ATV routes and some viewpoints may be closed.
Mayon is most visible early in the morning. If photography is your goal, arrive at Cagsawa or the Legazpi coast around sunrise.
Since several ATV operators compete for business, compare routes, duration, riders per vehicle, and whether helmets and masks are provided.
There's a lot of volcanic ash dust during the ATV tour. Bring a mask, sunglasses, disposable clothing, and long pants.
Downtown Legazpi has many ATMs and malls, but around Camalig or Cagsawa, most places accept cash only.
It rains often, so always carry an umbrella or raincoat.
If the food is too spicy for you, asking for it "less spicy" will usually be accommodated.
If it's whale shark season in Donsol, it's easy to combine a day trip there from a base in Legazpi.

When the alert level rises, viewpoints inside the 6 km zone, such as Mayon Skyline (Tabaco), close, but outer viewing points such as Legazpi Boulevard, the Cagsawa Ruins, the front of Daraga Church, Sumlang Lake, and Quitinday Hills are generally open. Ask your hotel or guide which ones are open that day.

Overnight buses have strong air conditioning, so you'll want a light jacket. Buses arrive in Legazpi between 8 and 11 AM, so letting your hotel know in advance makes it easier to drop off your luggage early.
The permanent danger zone within a
6 km
radius of the summit is off-limits regardless of alert level. Never attempt to climb with an unofficial guide. In
, an unannounced steam explosion during a climb killed five people, including a foreign climber and a guide.
When the alert level rises, nearby residents are evacuated and roads are closed. Always prioritize following local authority guidance.
On days with heavy ash fall, people with respiratory conditions and children should limit outdoor activity and wear an N95 mask.
After heavy rain, lahar can occur in streams on the volcano's slopes. Don't linger in riverbeds or dry gullies.
During typhoon season (
September–December
), flights and buses can be canceled, so build extra time into your schedule.
The alert level is Level 2 as of
September 2026
, but sulfur dioxide emissions have increased again and weak eruptions have been observed at the summit, so it could rise to Level 3 at any time. Check the latest bulletin on the
official PHIVOLCS website
right before you set off.
Mayon is a volcano that is still alive today. Never forget that danger lies behind the beautiful scenery — check official alerts and enjoy it only from permitted areas.
